catalog.name: SpectralBL-Analytics Dataset Catalog
catalog.description: Catalog of boundary layer meteorological field campaigns, SCM benchmarks, and diagnostic assets for GeoABL.jl.

status_definitions.Ingested: Dataset fully processed into GeoABL.jl AtmosphericColumnDataset format.
status_definitions.Potential Future Use: Candidate observational campaign queued for schema mapping and ingestion.

notes: GABLS3 serves as the core nocturnal boundary layer baseline.
CASES-99 target dataset for verifying precursor lead time (dt_fold).
SHEBA provides multi-level polar pack ice boundary layer profiles and surface roughness estimations.

framework_role.structural_purpose: Single-Column Model benchmark for low-level jet formation and inversion strength.

site_description.details: 200-meter mast providing continuous profiles of wind speed, direction, potential temperature, and specific humidity.

meteorological_conditions.key_features: Strong Nocturnal Low-Level Jet, radiative surface cooling
meteorological_conditions.transition_dynamics: Rapid evening boundary layer collapse followed by persistent nocturnal jet formation

primary_papers: Baas et al. (2010) - Unraveling the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
Bosveld et al. (2014) - The Third GABLS Model Intercomparison

framework_role.structural_purpose: Validation of fold precursor lead time (dt_fold) prior to nocturnal collapse events.

site_description.details: Main 60m tower equipped with high-frequency sonic anemometers and thermocouples across 8 vertical levels.

meteorological_conditions.key_features: Intermittent turbulence, strong shear, nocturnal temperature inversions
meteorological_conditions.transition_dynamics: Evening transition driven by rapid decay of surface heat flux

primary_papers: Poulos et al. (2002) - CASES-99 Field Experiment Overview
Sun et al. (2002) - Physical Processes in the Stable Boundary Layer
literature_context.notes: Focused on October 1999 nighttime intensive observation periods (IOPs).

datasets.name: SHEBA Atmospheric Surface Flux Group (Met City)

location.specific_site: Ice Station SHEBA Met City Mast (75°N–80°N drift)

framework_role.structural_purpose: Primary benchmark for perennial sea-ice momentum exchange, dynamic roughness estimation (z0m, z0h, z0q), and radiative cooling budgets.

site_description.details: 5-level tower (z1–z5) measuring wind speed, temperature, humidity, 3D sonic turbulence, and surface radiative fluxes.

meteorological_conditions.key_features: Strong persistent winter inversions, Arctic air-ice-sea coupling, low moisture flux
meteorological_conditions.stability_regime: Very stable to weakly convective transition
meteorological_conditions.transition_dynamics: Seasonal drift transitions from October 1997 through October 1998

data_assets.ingestion_source: NCAR/EOL Dataset 13.114 (https://doi.org/10.5065/D65H7DNS); prof_file_all6_ed_hd.txt & main_file6_hd.txt -> prof_file_all6.nc & main_file6.nc via scripts/SHEBAprof2nc.jl

primary_papers: Andreas et al. (1999) - An Overview of the SHEBA Atmospheric Flux Program
Persson et al. (2002) - Measurements Near the Atmospheric Surface Flux Group Tower at SHEBA
literature_context.notes: Citation: Andreas, E., et al. 2007. Tower, 5-level hourly measurements plus radiometer and surface data at Met City (ASFG). NSF NCAR EOL. https://doi.org/10.5065/D65H7DNS. Ingested using scripts/SHEBAprof2nc.jl; roughness calculated with Buck (1981) ice saturation thermodynamics.
